Q: Please state your full name for the recording.
A: I'd rather just say I'm the driver of the blue sedan. You can note my details from the file.
Q: Understood. Can you describe where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was in Pasadena, Texas, heading down a two-lane road in the early afternoon. Traffic was light and I was going
maybe twenty-five miles an hour.
Q: What happened next?
A: The other car drifted into my lane and we hit nearly head-on. It wasn't a big impact, more like a hard shove. Both
cars came to a stop almost right away.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before it crossed into your lane?
A: Not really. I saw headlights coming, and then they were already in front of me. I braked and turned the wheel, but
there wasn't time to do much.
Q: Were you injured?
A: My left wrist hit the steering wheel and the airbag went off. The pain was bad right away. They took me to the
hospital and the doctor said the wrist was fractured. I've got a cast on it now and I'm wearing a brace when I'm not
sleeping.
Q: Have you been able to work since the accident?
A: Not in my usual job. I drive for a living and I can't grip the wheel for long stretches with this cast, so I'm on leave for
now.
Q: Did you receive any treatment beyond the hospital visit?
A: Yes, I've been to my family doctor and I'm scheduled with a hand specialist next week. I'm keeping all the
paperwork together.
Q: Is there anything else you would like to add?
A: Only that I'm cooperating fully and I'd appreciate a call when you've reviewed the other driver's statement.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
A: Thank you.
</page>

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
